hints.content:
We can make a right triangle where the hypotenuse of the triangle is the given line. We can represent the length of the line with $\greenD x$:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: The first quadrant of an x- y- coordinate plane. A line segment extends from two, two to eight, five. A dashed horizontal line extends six units then vetrically three units to eight, five to form a right triangle. The hypotenuse is x.

hints.content:
Now we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find $\greenD x$:

$\begin{align} \maroonD a^2 + \maroonD b^2 &= \greenD x^2 ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{The Pythagorean theorem}}\\\\
\maroonD{6}^2 + \maroonD{3}^2 &= \greenD{x}^2 ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Plug in the side lengths}}\\\\
36+ 9&= \greenD x^2 ~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Evaluate } 6^2 \text{ and }  3^2}\\\\
45 &= \greenD x^2~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Add 36 and 9}}\\\\
\greenD x &=\sqrt{45}~~~~~~~~\small\gray{\text{Take the square root of each side}}\\\\ \\\end{align}$

###The answer

The length of the line is $\sqrt{45}$ units.
